title: OpenGardenRack spec
description: I2C daisy-chain protocol for stacked garden modules: wires at the top, data at the bottom

children.title: Electrical
children.description: docs/01-electrical.md: rails, logic levels, bus speed, chain limits
children.details:
Source: `docs/01-electrical.md`

- **Logic:** 5V on `SDA`, `SCL`, `EN`. 5V is *not* on the connector: each module regulates it from 12V.
- **System power:** 12V for actuators (pumps, fans, LEDs). Common GND is mandatory.
- **Bus speed:** fixed 100 kbps (Standard mode).
- **Limits:** up to 3 m chain height and **12 modules** per electrical segment (400 pF budget, ~60 pF/m cable). Longer or denser chains need a bus buffer/repeater.
- **Pull-ups:** 2.2 kΩ, only at the master.

children.title: Connector
children.details:
Source: `docs/02-connector.md`

- **Pins:** 1 `12V`, 2 `GND`, 3 `SDA`, 4 `SCL`, 5 `EN`.
- Every module has **two connectors**: bottom carries `EN_IN`, top carries `EN_OUT`. Power and I2C pass straight through.
- Consequence: removing a module disconnects everything stacked above it. Enumeration and hot-plug rules rely on this.

children.title: Boot sequence
children.details:
Source: `docs/03-enumeration.md` §3.1

1. All nodes hold `EN_OUT` low.
2. Master raises `EN` for the bottom module.
3. The enabled node answers on default address `0x08`; master reads `CLASS` and writes `SET_ADDR`.
4. Master waits **≥50 ms**, then verifies by reading `PROT_VER` at the new address (non-blocking; see `OgrMaster` in `ogr-main`).
5. Node raises `EN_OUT`, enabling the next module. Stops when nothing answers on `0x08`.

Registration order **is** physical order: the address itself carries no position.

children.title: Module states
children.details:
Source: `docs/03-enumeration.md` §3.2

- **UNASSIGNED** — answers on `0x08`; registration runs.
- **OK** — answers on its address, `STATUS = 0`.
- **PROBLEM** — ACKs but `STATUS ≠ 0`, or times out N times. Kept in the table.
- **REMOVED** — NACK on the address K times. Address freed.

PROBLEM vs REMOVED is exactly ACK-with-bad-content vs NACK-on-address.

children.title: Scan cycles
children.details:
Source: `docs/03-enumeration.md` §3.3

- **Health-check** (frequent): read `STATUS` of every known address → REMOVED / PROBLEM.
- **Scan-for-new** (frequent): only `0x08`, picks up hot-plugged or cascaded modules.
- **Full-range** (rare, and always once at master start): finds orphaned modules that hold an address the master does not know.

children.title: RESTART and orphans
children.details:
Source: `docs/03-enumeration.md` §3.4–3.6

- `RESTART` makes a node forget its address and drop `EN_OUT`, so **everything above it** cascades back to UNASSIGNED. This is normal, not a fault.
- **Orphan recovery:** the master restarts known modules from the top down until the orphan stops answering, then re-registers them in physical order. Adopting the orphan in place was rejected (ADR-0004).
- **Known limitation:** a fully hung node looks like REMOVED; `RESTART` cannot reach it.

children.title: Transactions
children.details:
Source: `docs/05-frame-format.md` §5.1–5.2

- Multi-byte values are **little-endian**.
- Write: `START, ADDR+W, REG, DATA…, PEC, STOP`.
- Read: `START, ADDR+W, REG, REPEATED START, ADDR+R, DATA…, PEC, STOP`.
- 1 byte for most system registers, up to 4 for the data window.

children.title: PEC and retries
children.details:
Source: `docs/05-frame-format.md` §5.3–5.4

- Every transaction ends with a **CRC-8/SMBUS** PEC (poly `0x07`, init `0x00`) over all bytes on the bus, both address bytes included.
- **Writes:** the node ACKs everything; on a bad PEC it discards the write and sets `STATUS = Error`. No in-band failure signal.
- **Reads:** on a bad PEC the master retries the whole transaction, 3 attempts. Three fully failed transactions push the module to PROBLEM.

children.title: System block
children.details:
Source: `docs/04-register-map.md` §4.1

- **0x00** `PROT_VER`, **0x01** `STATUS` (0 OK, 1 Error, 2 Busy), **0x02** `CLASS`, **0x03** `EP_COUNT`
- **0x04** `SYS_FLAGS`: bit 0 `IS_ANCHOR`, bit 1 `HAS_BLUEPRINT`
- **0x05** `SET_ADDR` (W), **0x06** `RESTART` (W: 1 soft, 2 hard)
- **0x07–0x0A** `PLANT_UID` (uint32; anchors must persist it in NVS/EEPROM; `0xFFFFFFFF` = none)
- **0x0B–0x0E** `BP_UID` blueprint ID
- **0x0F** `EP_SELECT`
- **0x10–0x1F** reserved

children.title: Endpoints
children.details:
Source: `docs/04-register-map.md` §4.2

- Write an index to `EP_SELECT` (0x0F); default 0 after addressing or restart. Index ≥ `EP_COUNT` is ignored and sets `STATUS = Error`.
- **0x20–0x22** descriptor of the selected endpoint: type ID, mode (R/W/RW), data format.
- **0x40–0x43** data window, 4 bytes, little-endian; narrower values use the low bytes.

children.title: CLASS IDs
children.details:
Source: `docs/06-class-ids.md`

- **0x01** Plant container (usually an anchor)
- **0x02** Light
- **0x03** Water supply
- **0x04** Climate
- **0xFF** Custom / unspecified

children.title: Type IDs
children.details:
Source: `docs/07-type-ids.md`

- **Sensors 0x40–0x7F:** moisture, temp (0.1 °C), humidity, light, weight, distance, water level
- **Actuators 0x80–0xBF:** relay, dimmer, water valve, light switch, water pump, vibro
- **Widgets 0xC0–0xFF:** camera (out-of-band stream)

children.title: ogr-main
children.details:
Repository: github.com/vvapnik/ogr-main, locally `code/core/ogr-main`.

Runs enumeration, scan cycles and orphan recovery from the head module. Target: ESP32 / S3 / C3.

children.title: ogr-node-core
children.details:
Repository: github.com/vvapnik/ogr-node-core, locally `code/core/ogr-node-core`.

Implements the register map, `EP_SELECT`, PEC and the EN chain for a node. A HAL package plugs it into a concrete MCU.

children.title: Node HALs
children.description: AVR, ESP32 Arduino, ESP32 IDF, CH32V003
children.details:
Source: `docs/08-libraries.md` (lists the public ones)

- **ogr-node-hal-avr** — ATmega328 (TWI), ATtiny85 (USI). Public.
- **ogr-node-hal-esp32-arduino** — ESP32 family on Arduino `Wire`. Public.
- **ogr-node-hal-esp32** — ESP-IDF. Private.
- **ogr-node-hal-ch32v003** — CH32V003. Private.

All libraries are AI-generated and hardware-tested, but not yet human-reviewed.

children.title: Light module
children.details:
- **CLASS:** `0x02` Light, `IS_ANCHOR = 0`
- **Stack position:** 7 (registered right after the pot below it)
- **Endpoints, for example:** `0x81` Dimmer (PWM), `0x43` Light sensor
- `PLANT_UID` is optional for a non-anchor module; if unsupported it reads `0xFFFFFFFF`.

children.title: Pot module
children.details:
- **CLASS:** `0x01` Plant container, `IS_ANCHOR = 1`
- **PLANT_UID:** `0x00000003`, stored in NVS/EEPROM so the plant keeps its identity across restarts
- **Stack position:** 6
- **Endpoints, for example:** `0x40` Moisture, `0x82` Water valve

children.title: Water tank
children.description: CLASS 0x03 Water Supply, bottom of the stack
children.details:
- **CLASS:** `0x03` Water supply, `IS_ANCHOR = 0`
- **Stack position:** 1 — the master enables it first, so it gets the first address
- **Endpoints, for example:** `0x84` Water pump, `0x46` Water level
- Sits at the bottom: every module above it gets power, I2C and `EN` through it.
